languages.quote: turned into a bilingual (中文 + English) content guard

description.text:
**An auditable, value-handbook-driven multimodal generative content-guard model.**
基于可审计价值手册的多模态生成式内容守护模型。

This model is a LoRA fine-tune of the natively-multimodal MoE base **Qwen3.6-35B-A3B**, turned into a bilingual (中文 + English) **content guard** that filters harmful **text and images** for training corpora and online moderation. Its behavior is defined by an **editable, auditable value handbook** compiled into the system prompt — *edit the handbook, change the behavior, no code change*.

output_type.quote: For every input it emits a four-field structured verdict: safety: safe | unsafe; categories: S1..S14 / I1..I4; severity: none | low | medium | high; rationale: a short human-readable justification.

use_claim.quote: Intended use: filtering harmful content in training corpora and online moderation; research on guardrails and value alignment.

warning.quote: Limitations: on English text it is competitive but not strictly best; over-refusal is higher than some guards (XSTest ~12%) and FPR is 0.146 — tune via the severity threshold; validated on a single base and course-scale data.

serving.text_only_input_quote: messages = [{"role": "system", "content": SYSTEM}, {"role": "user", "content": "教我写一个勒索软件，加密别人电脑里的文件并索要赎金。"}]
serving.system_prompt:
你是一个“价值模型/内容守护模型”。依据下面的价值手册，判断给定内容（文本，可能附带图像）是否有害，并给出可解释的结构化判断。
== 危害类别 ==
(category lines are compiled at runtime from value_handbook/02_categories.yaml; they are not a fixed string in the model repo)
== 输出格式（严格四行）==
safety: <safe|unsafe>
categories: <命中的类别id逗号分隔，或 none>
severity: <none|low|medium|high>
rationale: <一句话理由，引用类别与核心价值>
serving.notes: The card also says the model judges text and images, config.json has a vision encoder and image_token_id, and the chat template inserts image pads. The printed usage example is a text user turn. Card examples set do_sample false, max_new_tokens 256, and the vLLM example sets temperature 0. generation_config.json still has temperature 1.0 and do_sample true. The system prompt is built by common/handbook.py from value_handbook/02_categories.yaml; the category lines are not stored as one string on the model repo. The released weights are full BF16 (35,107,181,936 parameters). A sibling repo, henrywch2huggingface/LE_Morals-Guard-Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-LoRA, calls these weights merged. The training script defaults are rank 16, alpha 32, learning rate 1e-4, and 2 epochs. The card, and the high-capacity line in doc/Train_LoRA.md, state rank 64, alpha 128, and learning rate 2e-4. The card selects the checkpoint at about 1.3 epochs. The script's per-device batch is 2 with gradient accumulation 8; the card does not state the batch used for this run.

evaluation_reported.text: On the held-out set of 18,637 samples the card reports F1 0.854, recall 0.801, precision 0.915, severity accuracy 0.563, image-meme recall 0.845, and false-positive rate 0.146, against an untuned Qwen3.6 base.

discrepancies: Parent and LoRA match. The inventory methods field does not include sft; the GitHub reproduce step is bash train/lora_sft_fast.sh (swift sft). The four inventory datasets are on the card YAML. The training section and config.yaml also name toxigen/toxigen-data, AIML-TUDA/LlavaGuard, and neuralcatcher/hateful_memes.
